711488.t: σάνδαλον (sándalon) + -ιον (-ion, diminutive), of uncertain origin, possibly loaned from Parthian, Persian, or another substrate of Asia Minor.

711420.t: From Proto-Hellenic *twálos, from Proto-Indo-European *tuh₂-(e)l-o- ~ *tweh₂-(e)l-o-, from *tewh₂- (“to swell; to crowd; to be strong”).

711424.t: Formation like σῦριγξ (sûrĭnx) and φόρμιγξ (phórmĭnx). As a word of Mediterranean culture, it remains without Indo-European connection.
